SPECIFICATION OF A UNIFORM STEEL TIE STRIP UNDER 6.00 kN STATIC TENSION

Available thicknesses: 2.00, 3.00, 4.00 mm. Gross-section axial stress only (sigma = P/A); holes, connections, self-weight, corrosion and dimensional tolerances ignored per the request.

Minimum required gross area: A_req = P / sigma_allow = 6000 N / 100 N/mm^2 = 60.0 mm^2, hence t_req = A_req / w = 60.0 / 20.0 = 3.00 mm.

--- 1. SELECTED DIMENSIONS ---
Thickness:      t = 3.00 mm (smallest available thickness that passes)
Width:          w = 20.0 mm
Length:         L = 500 mm
Gross area:     A = w x t = 20.0 x 3.00 = 60.0 mm^2
Section shape:  uniform rectangular strip, constant section over the full 500 mm length

--- 2. STRENGTH CHECK (gross section, sigma = P/A) ---
Allowable: sigma_allow = 100 MPa = 100 N/mm^2.

  t = 2.00 mm (next thinner available): A = 20.0 x 2.00 = 40.0 mm^2
      sigma = 6000 / 40.0 = 150 MPa  ->  150 MPa > 100 MPa  ->  FAILS
      (exceeds the allowable by 50 MPa, i.e. utilisation 1.50)

  t = 3.00 mm (SELECTED): A = 20.0 x 3.00 = 60.0 mm^2
      sigma = 6000 / 60.0 = 100.0 MPa  ->  100.0 MPa = 100 MPa  ->  PASSES
      (utilisation 1.00; equality with the allowable is permitted by the specification,
       so this is a compliant, zero-margin result by gross-section stress alone)

  t = 4.00 mm (for reference, not selected): A = 20.0 x 4.00 = 80.0 mm^2
      sigma = 6000 / 80.0 = 75.0 MPa  ->  PASSES (utilisation 0.75, heavier than needed)

Verdict: the 2.00 mm strip fails at 150 MPa; the 3.00 mm strip passes at exactly 100.0 MPa. Therefore 3.00 mm is the smallest available thickness that satisfies the 100 MPa allowable with equality permitted.

--- 3. VOLUME AND MASS OF THE SELECTED STRIP (t = 3.00 mm) ---
Volume:  V = w x t x L = 20.0 mm x 3.00 mm x 500 mm = 30 000 mm^3
            = 30.0 cm^3 = 3.00 x 10^-5 m^3
Mass:    m = rho x V = 7850 kg/m^3 x 3.00 x 10^-5 m^3 = 0.2355 kg = 235.5 g
         (equivalently 30.0 cm^3 x 7.85 g/cm^3 = 235.5 g)
Mass per unit length (for handling reference only): 0.2355 kg / 0.500 m = 0.471 kg/m.
